title: Navan Edge vs. Otto: Which is better for business travel?
summary: Compare Navan Edge and Otto for booking, loyalty, trip changes, human help, rental cars, restaurants, and the way you travel for work.
body_markdown:
Navan Edge and Otto both use AI to plan and book individual business trips from a plain-language request, but they’re built around different ways of working. Navan Edge keeps planning, booking, loyalty context, restaurant reservations where available, trip changes, and 24/7 human help within a dedicated travel experience. Otto brings booking into more of the tools you already use, with calendar-led planning, rental cars, and price monitoring for eligible refundable reservations.\[1\]\[3\]\[4\]


This guide compares how the two platforms handle bookings, loyalty and preferences, access, post-booking support, and human handoffs. By the end, you’ll have a practical way to decide which one better fits the trips you actually take — not simply which has the longer feature list.


## Key takeaways


- Navan Edge is likely the stronger fit for an individual business traveler who wants loyalty status, personal preferences, restaurant planning, and 24/7 human help connected to the same trip thread.
- Otto has a credible advantage when the trip includes a rental car or when you want to book through Slack, Microsoft Teams, or an MCP-compatible assistant.\[1\]\[3\]
- Both products remember preferences, book real travel, require approval before a transaction or change, and offer human support.


## Navan Edge vs. Otto at a glance


Navan Edge and Otto are both AI travel assistants that can book flights and hotels, remember your preferences, require confirmation before completing transactions, and connect you with human support.


Navan Edge centers the experience in one dedicated travel conversation, with loyalty visibility and restaurant reservations where available. Otto works across a broader range of tools and adds calendar context, rental-car booking, and price-drop monitoring for eligible refundable reservations.\[1\]\[3\]\[4\] The table below shows how those differences translate into day-to-day use.

The differences become clearer when a trip adds a loyalty target, client dinner, calendar constraint, rental car, or change that needs human judgment.\[1\]\[2\]\[3\]\[4\]\[5\]


## What’s the main difference between Navan Edge and Otto?


Navan Edge concentrates the trip inside a dedicated travel app. Your[stated preferences, booking history, and connected loyalty programs](https://navan.com/product/navan-edge) shape the options that are surfaced, while the trip and support conversation stay connected in one thread. That model suits someone who wants the assistant to have full context of their business travel, not just complete the current transaction.


Otto distributes the booking experience across tools. It connects to Google or Microsoft calendars and can work through Slack, Microsoft Teams, and MCP-compatible assistants such as ChatGPT or Claude.\[1\] Which is useful if the convenience you care about is booking without leaving your work conversation.


Put simply, Navan Edge is organized around one ongoing travel conversation. Otto is organized around making the travel agent available in more of your existing conversations. That difference affects every other part of the comparison.


## Can both tools book a full work trip?


Both can book flights and hotels. From there, their definitions of a “full trip” diverge.


Imagine you’re heading to Chicago for a Tuesday morning meeting. You need a flight that gets you there by Monday evening, a hotel near the client, dinner for four, and enough flexibility to move the return flight if the meeting runs late. You can explain exactly this scenario to Navan Edge, and it can work through the[flight, hotel, and restaurant in one chat](https://navan.com/terms/edge-services-agreement) . You can mention very specific preferences and connect loyalty programs, and it presents options from live inventory. Navan Edge will never book or change anything without[your explicit confirmation](https://navan.com/product/navan-edge) .


That connected experience continues after checkout. You can return to the same conversation with itinerary questions or change requests, and bring in a 24/7 human travel agent when the situation requires judgment. Restaurant reservations, where available, are one part of that broader model: Navan Edge keeps the trip’s context, bookings, loyalty information, changes, and human support together.


Otto takes a different approach to trip coverage. It books flights, hotels, and rental cars, uses connected Google or Microsoft calendars to shape recommendations, and works through the web, mobile apps, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and compatible AI assistants. That can make Otto a strong fit when a rental car is essential or the itinerary needs to be organized closely around existing meetings.


## Which is better for loyalty rewards, Navan Edge or Otto?


Navan Edge is likely the better choice for frequent travelers who want loyalty information to influence which flights and hotels they book. Both products can remember loyalty numbers and travel preferences, but Navan Edge uses that context more broadly when evaluating a trip.


The[Navan Edge Loyalty Wallet](https://navan.com/terms/edge-loyalty-program) brings supported airline and hotel programs into one place, where you can track estimated points, miles, and progress toward your next status tier. Navan Edge can also use your connected programs, booking history, and preferences shared in chat to personalize its recommendations. This helps you evaluate not only which option works, but which one supports your longer-term loyalty goals.


[Otto](https://www.ottotheagent.com/product) focuses on applying saved information automatically. You add your airline, hotel, and rental-car loyalty numbers and preferences once, and Otto carries them into supported bookings. It also maps airline alliances and identifies hotel channels or rates that may not earn points.\[2\] That helps reduce repeated data entry and avoid missed loyalty credit.


The difference is that Otto helps apply your loyalty details, while Navan Edge helps you actively manage and use them. If loyalty status, reward balances, and repeat preferences regularly shape your travel decisions, Navan Edge may offer the more complete experience.


## How do Navan Edge and Otto manage your trip after booking?


Both assistants remain available after confirmation, but their emphasis is on different things. Navan Edge’s post-booking advantage is continuity. Your itinerary remains in the same travel conversation, so you can check details, ask follow-up questions, or request changes without rebuilding the context as your plans evolve.


Otto adds more proactive monitoring. It watches booked trips for delays, cancellations, and schedule changes and can prepare rebooking options for your approval. It also monitors eligible fully refundable flights and fully refundable, pay-at-property hotel rooms for price drops. If it finds a lower price, Otto alerts you and waits for approval before canceling and rebooking.\[1\]\[3\]


Price monitoring has specific limits, however. Basic economy and other nonrefundable fares aren’t eligible, and the reservation must have been booked through Otto.\[3\]


## Do Navan Edge and Otto provide human support?


Both products can connect you with a person, but the service models are different.


Navan Edge includes[24/7 access to human travel experts](https://navan.com/product/navan-edge) in the same conversation thread where you made your bookings, so the agent has complete context of your trip and preferences. You can ask a human to enter the chat at any moment, keeping the request and itinerary inside the same travel experience. You don’t need to move to a separate channel or reconstruct the request.


Otto’s human assistance is provided by Direct Travel. Before transferring the conversation, Otto prepares the confirmation numbers, trip details, a summary of the request, and a recommended action for the agent. Help is available 24/7.\[4\]


For travelers who prioritise continuity, Navan Edge is the stronger choice in this category.


## Navan Edge or Otto: Which should you choose?


Choose Navan Edge if you want one travel companion to carry context across the whole trip. It brings your preferences, booking history, loyalty progress, flight and hotel planning, restaurant reservations, itinerary changes, and human assistance into one unified conversation. Navan Edge’s focus is on maintaining a connected travel experience.


Otto may fit better when rental-car booking, calendar-led recommendations, access through other tools in your tech stack, or price monitoring drives the decision. Test the difference with a real upcoming trip. Give Navan Edge your schedule, loyalty programs, hotel requirements, and dining plans, then see how well it uses that context to build and manage the trip.[Try Navan Edge with your next work trip](https://navan.com/get-started-edge) .
